paras: Oldham's bow-fingered gecko (Cyrtodactylus oldhami) is a species of lizard in the family Gekkonidae. The species is native to Myanmar and Thailand.
Both the specific name, oldhami, and the common name, Oldham's bow-fingered gecko, are in honor of English plant collector Richard Oldham (1837–1864).
Cyrtodactylus oldhami is found in southern Myanmar and southern Thailand.
The preferred natural habitat of Cyrtodactylus oldhami is forest, at altitudes from sea level to 150 m (490 ft).
Cyrtodactylus oldhami may attain a snout-to-vent length (SVL) of 6.5 cm (2.6 in), plus a tail 7.5 cm (3.0 in) long.
